name: Trust & safety / livestream moderation
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Generic real-time stack overwhelmingly dominated by Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / HLL / Top-K / T-Digest modules — Redis 8.0 May 2025 promoted these to first-class ACL categories @bloom / @cms / @topk / @tdigest). Every T&S team interviewed publicly cites Redis as the default: Reddit Anti-Evil, Discord T&S (whose Counter service is described in the Osprey blog as 'heavily integrated with internal Scylla databases'), Twitch chat (token-bucket buckets per channel), Bluesky pre-Osprey. Aerospike at very high cardinality (Roblox, Sony PSN). Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers with a Kafka backbone — RisingWave publishes an explicit 'Real-time features for Account Takeover' blog whose shape is identical for T&S. Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel-now-Databricks for managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost / transformer toxicity / spam / grooming-risk models. Custom in-Rust / in-Elixir services on RocksDB / Sled at Discord and Twitch scale. GetStream Chat as a hosted real-time-chat substrate with built-in moderation (5M-concurrent-connection benchmark). Postgres + materialized views at the small end (Bluesky's Ozone moderation UI is Next.js + PostgreSQL). NEW IN 2025: Osprey (Discord, donated to ROOST July 2025, v1.0 GA) is the open-source RULES ENGINE layer — a Rust coordinator + stateless Python workers running SML rules at 2.3M rules/sec and 400M actions/day at Discord, 45-50M events/day at Bluesky. Osprey is explicitly NOT a feature/counter store: it tracks entity labels via a pluggable 'labels service' backend (Postgres reference impl) and reaches counters via UDFs that RPC out to external services (Discord's internal Scylla-backed Counter service is mentioned but NOT open-sourced). The feature backend underneath Osprey is the slot beava actually competes for.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific named incumbents for livestream + UGC T&S, 2024-2026 status. End-to-end T&S vendors (the buyer procures these as black boxes that internally subsume the feature-store layer): Hive AI (Hive Moderation; 75+ customers including Reddit, Yubo, Chatroulette, Omegle, Tango; livestream-platform vertical page; Series D $85M April 2021 at $2B; reported seeking $200M at $4B valuation in Aug 2023 [uncertain — no later raise publicly confirmed]; DoD deepfake-detection contract Dec 2024). ActiveFence -> Alice (rebranded January 2026; ~$100M total raised through 2021 Series B at $500M+ valuation; acquired Spectrum Labs September 2023; acquired Rewire; 7% layoff March 2025; now 'Alice' protects 3B+ users + 7 of 10 largest AI foundation models — Amazon, TikTok, ByteDance, Nvidia, Cohere, Black Forest Labs; pivoted to GenAI model security while keeping classic T&S). Modulate / ToxMod (voice; $30M Series A 2022 from Lakestar; deployed at Call of Duty: MWIII/Warzone/Black Ops 6 — toxicity exposure -25%, repeat-offender rate -43% in BO6 / -38% in Warzone, ~2M voice-chat enforcement actions since Dec 2024; RecRoom, Discord Social SDK integration; >160M hours moderated to date; Italian, AU/NZ rollout 2025). Cinder ($14M total — Accel-led $10M Series A + $4M seed; YC W22; AWS GenAI Accelerator, Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, Mozilla Ventures; 30 employees; positioning as 'infrastructure to protect companies from AI abuse'). TrustLab ($15M Series A 2023; DSA/OSA/AOSA compliance focus; ex-Google/Reddit/ByteDance team). Resolver (security/risk/compliance, 1000+ orgs). Sift Content Integrity (part of Digital Trust & Safety suite, 1T events/year; G2 #1 in fraud-related categories 2025 Summer Reports; Q2 2025 Digital Trust Index report — NOT merged with Spectrum Labs; Spectrum Labs was acquired by ActiveFence/Alice in Sept 2023, not Sift). Microsoft Community Sift (acquired Two Hat; Xbox / Roblox embedded). Sumsub (identity + AI-Agent Verification 2025-2026). Lasso, Checkstep, VoicePatrol, MediaFirewall (livestream-specific). GetStream Chat (chat substrate + integrated rate limiting). Agora SDK + bundled ActiveFence integration. NEW: ROOST (non-profit, July 2025) shipped Osprey (rules engine, donated by Discord) AND Coop (case-management + NCMEC reporting + HMA hash matching, acquired from Cove) — these two together are an OSS replica of what Cinder / TrustLab / ActiveFence sell, and Bluesky has adopted Osprey in production. In-house equivalents: Reddit Anti-Evil + Safety Signals; Discord T&S (Osprey origin); Twitch Safety (AutoMod + Shield Mode + Suspicious User Detection + 2025 Verified Chats); Roblox Safety Engineering (Sentinel open-sourced August 2025 — contrastive-learning grooming-risk classifier, 1,200 NCMEC reports H1 2025, 35% caught before user report; voice abuse reports/DAU cut in half); YouTube Live T&S (Google ML stack); TikTok / ByteDance live stack; Activision player-safety (ToxMod + Community Sift); Riot Vanguard; Bluesky T&S (Osprey + Ozone + 24/7 ops; 9.97M reports / 16.49M labels / 2.45M removals in 2025; 41.4M users by end-2025; 1,470 legal requests up from 238 in 2024). Beava sits UNDERNEATH any of these — not against them.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and shifting decisively toward OSS in 2025-2026. (a) Rules-engine layer: Apache-2.0 OSS now leads — Osprey (Apache-2.0, ROOST), Coop (open source, ROOST), Roblox Sentinel (open source, Aug 2025). This is a recent and important shift: the rules engine — historically a Cinder/TrustLab/ActiveFence proprietary moat — has been commoditised by Discord + Bluesky + Roblox donations. (b) Feature/counter backend underneath: split. Redis 7.4+ RSALv2/SSPLv1 (non-OSI, Fedora/Debian/Ubuntu treat as non-OSS); Redis 8 (May 2025) added back AGPLv3 as part of tri-license. Valkey (BSD-3-Clause, LF, AWS/Google/Oracle, ships as default 'redis' in Ubuntu 26.04) is the procurement-clean fork. (c) End-to-end T&S vendors (Hive, Alice/ActiveFence, Modulate, Cinder, TrustLab, Sift, Microsoft Community Sift, Sumsub, Lasso, Checkstep): uniformly proprietary SaaS. Beava's Apache-2.0 + no-open-core posture is a real wedge specifically as the counter/feature backend under an Osprey/Coop stack — a buyer or T&S vendor that picks Osprey (Apache-2.0) for rules then needs an Apache-2.0 counter backend to avoid the Redis license re-litigation. License posture is now a hard procurement filter, especially for ROOST-aligned T&S buyers.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium. Lower than bot-defence (V3) and edge/CDN (V9) where Cloudflare bundles the whole stack, but non-trivial. Three vectors. (1) AWS-bundled paths: Modulate / ToxMod scales on AWS and is repeatedly co-marketed via AWS GameTech blog; Cinder is in the AWS GenAI Accelerator; Coop runs on hyperscaler infra; HMA (hash-matching, MetaCAi -> ROOST June 2025) is essentially a free service. (2) Microsoft / Azure: Community Sift (post-Two-Hat acquisition) is embedded across Xbox / Azure Communication Services — a default for buyers already on Azure. (3) Discord Social SDK + ToxMod is a packaged integration for any game using Discord auth/voice, which is functionally a vendor bundle for the embedded-voice case. BUT — the buyer in T&S genuinely runs in their own VPC for legal-residency / DSA-data-control reasons; they cannot offload to a SaaS for the velocity-feature path; and the ROOST stack (Osprey + Coop) explicitly demands a self-hosted feature backend. Net: HIGH within the embedded-game / embedded-voice / SaaS-T&S-vendor sub-segment; LOW-to-MEDIUM for any in-house T&S team at a sovereign EU / UK / large in-house ROOST-adopting platform, which is exactly beava's realistic wedge.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Producers are the post / chat / DM / report / voice-classifier event paths, NOT Kafka-by-default — this is a fit for beava's push-on-event HTTP/TCP model. Expected upstreams: post-submit / comment-submit / DM-send service (the app server itself, HTTP POST), chat ingest (Twitch IRC / TMI WebSocket, Discord Gateway, TikTok Live WebSocket, YouTube Live Chat API, Kick chat, Bigo chat, GetStream Chat webhooks, Agora chat), AT Protocol firehose (Bluesky relay), Mastodon ActivityPub federation, WebRTC media-plane sidecars pushing voice_flag events from Modulate ToxMod / Hive Voice / Roblox Sentinel / in-house Whisper-based classifiers, moderation reporting endpoints (one HTTP POST per report), AutoMod / AutoModerator / Ozone labeler pipelines, viewer-presence service. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits webhooks and app-server producers; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput chat / voice gateways during raids. Kafka shows up at the big-in-house-platform tier (Reddit, X, TikTok internally) and is the natural shape for Osprey (which prefers Kafka-fed firehose — Bluesky's osprey-atproto adapter is literally 'a Go firehose-to-Kafka producer'), so a Kafka source connector for beava is a future fit but not v0 friction. Consumers: rules engines (Osprey above all in the new OSS world; AutoMod / AutoModerator YAML; in-house Drools / FEEL; Twitch 'Suspicious User Controls'; Cinder workflow engine; Hive auto-rules), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM for spam, Perspective and Hive transformers for toxicity, Sentinel for grooming-risk, ToxMod for voice toxicity), and inline action surfaces (slow-mode, followers-only, sub-only, unique-chat, emote-only, kick, timeout, ban, demote-from-stage, shadow-mute, label-overlay).
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with a heavier deterministic-rules tilt than payments fraud because livestream moderation actions (slow-mode / followers-only) must fire on simple, explainable thresholds in seconds. Buyers run rules (Osprey SML, AutoMod YAML, AutoModerator YAML, Twitch 'Suspicious User Controls', Hive auto-rules, in-house DSL — 'if room.unique_sender_count_10s > N AND new_account_pct > M then auto-followers-only') alongside ML scorers (Hive content moderation, Perspective toxicity, Sentinel grooming-risk contrastive classifier, ToxMod voice toxicity, in-house XGBoost spam). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer — both the rules engine (Osprey UDF calling into beava batch_get) and the ML model read from the same path. Crucially: Osprey by design has no built-in counter / aggregation primitives — UDFs reach out to external services — so the seam is structurally OPEN for beava.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Eight concrete reasons a buyer would pick beava over Redis-on-Lua or a SaaS vendor in this segment, sharpened by the 2025-2026 ROOST-driven shift. (1) Slot under Osprey: Osprey (Apache-2.0, Discord-origin, donated to ROOST, in production at Bluesky 45-50M events/day, processing 2.3M rules/sec at Discord 400M actions/day) is the rules engine that just won the OSS T&S layer — and it explicitly has NO built-in counter/feature backend; UDFs RPC out to external state services (Discord's Scylla-backed 'Counter service' was kept proprietary). Beava is the natural Apache-2.0 substitute for that internal Counter service in any non-Discord Osprey deployment. This is the cleanest single wedge of any segment in the matrix. (2) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the per-PoP / per-region / per-relay / per-channel-server sidecar topology that Bluesky-AT-Proto, Mastodon, Discord-shard, and Twitch-per-channel actually use. (3) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (counters, n_unique HLL, velocity, rate, distribution, distance, entropy, last-N) directly cover the velocity / report-storm / chat-burst / unique-reporter / per-(reporter,target) features T&S literally lives on — WITHOUT writing Lua, SML UDFs, or Flink SQL. The (reporter_id, target_id) and (sender_id, room_id) composite-key grains are first-class via @bv.table, not hand-rolled Redis hash-of-hash. (4) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the seconds-budget of live moderation: Roblox's published 15-second-end-to-end voice-action SLO is achievable with beava-level feature latency but tight on a Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline (typical 5-30s freshness). (5) Apache-2.0, no open-core — attractive to ROOST-aligned buyers (Bluesky, Matrix.org, any platform adopting Osprey) who do not want a Redis Source-Available dependency under their freshly-OSS rules engine, and attractive to T&S vendors (Cinder, TrustLab, Hive Live, Modulate) who want to embed it rather than depend on a competitor's managed cloud. (6) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how chat ingest, WebRTC media paths, and voice-classifier sidecars already shape events. (7) Distance primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel for raid-coordination signals and account-sharing across regions. (8) The ephemeral-grain shape (stream_id, lobby_id, stage_session_id born and dying with the broadcast) plus TTL eviction maps naturally to the live-moderation lifecycle — distinct from batch feature stores (Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk) that target stable entity types.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete current gaps blocking adoption in this segment (derived directly from use cases 9 + 9b open-engineering-gaps lists, sharpened to the Osprey-era buyer): (1) No TLS / no auth in v0 on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for ANY production deployment by a DSA-regulated platform (transparency reporting under Implementing Regulation 2025/1714, first reports collected from 1 July 2025), an Ofcom-regulated platform (UK OSA illegal-harms duties live 17 March 2025; children's-safety duties live 25 July 2025; first £1M fine issued to AVS Group, Kick under investigation), or a SOC-2-required T&S-vendor procurement. Single biggest blocker. (2) No triggers / 'fire callback when (room).unique_sender_count_10s crosses N' — live moderation is fundamentally event-driven on a seconds budget; polling 10-30 features per chat_message at livestream EPS just to threshold them is wasteful. This is the #2 most-cited gap and matters MORE here than in static UGC because the action surface (slow-mode, followers-only) is so tightly coupled to threshold-crossing. (3) No in-process sharding — Twitch / YouTube Live / TikTok Live / Roblox / Discord / Bluesky-at-current-scale exceed a single box at ~684k EPS / ~100 GB hot state; raid bursts can briefly push a single channel-server beyond a node. (4) Refuse-on-network-FS + in-memory-only means buyers must plan local-disk WAL and bound cold-start replay; a node restart during an active hate raid (which complete in <16s per CSCW 2023 academic data on Twitch raids) is an outage when seconds count. (5) No prominently-documented HLL / CMS / Top-K / T-Digest first-class promotion for the (room_id, sender_id) / (room_id, ip_asn) / (room_id, fp) cardinality-explosion paths — Redis Stack 8.0 promoted these to first-class @bloom / @cms / @topk / @tdigest ACL categories in May 2025 and beava must match. (6) No multi-tenancy primitives (namespaces, quotas, per-tenant rate-limit accounting) — every embedding T&S vendor (Cinder, TrustLab, Lasso, Checkstep, Modulate, Hive, Alice-ex-ActiveFence) needs this to serve many customers from one cluster. (7) No secondary indexes / no 'top-K rooms by chat velocity in last 10s' query — the live-SOC analyst dashboard surface (Twitch / Discord / Roblox / TikTok consoles all expose this). (8) No first-class session-window primitive tied to stream_start / stream_end — 'unique chatters in THIS broadcast' is a load-bearing concept that is neither tumbling nor sliding. (9) No graph / pair-clustering primitives for coordinated-raid detection (Meta CIB URL-sharing-time-similarity graphs). (10) No documented CSAM / PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash integration pattern — orthogonal but buyers expect a story for how beava composes with Coop / HMA (now hosted by ROOST since June 2025). (11) No native PII / voice-biometric handling story (IP-hash-at-rest, configurable retention, right-to-erasure cascading) — GDPR Art. 9 special-category-data treatment for voice biometric markers is load-bearing under DSA + UK OSA + CA AADC. (12) No Kafka source connector — Osprey-style deployments are Kafka-fed (Bluesky's osprey-atproto adapter is literally a firehose-to-Kafka producer), and beava's HTTP/TCP-push model is fine for direct app-server producers but mid-friction for the Osprey-standard topology.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo. The disqualifier list maps cleanly onto a 3-6 month engineering plan that is mostly infrastructure additions rather than data-model rewrites: TLS + token/mTLS auth (item 1) ~1mo; threshold-crossing triggers / webhooks (item 2) ~1-2mo and unlocks the most-cited domain gap; HLL/CMS/Top-K first-class promotion + documentation (item 5) ~2-4 weeks if already present; per-tenant namespaces + quotas + per-key TTL (items 6,4) ~1-2mo; session-window primitive (item 8) ~2-4 weeks; Kafka source connector (item 12) ~2-4 weeks. In-process sharding (item 3) is 6-12mo+ but not required for the realistic first wedge (single-region beava-under-Osprey for a Bluesky-class deployment fits in one box; only Twitch / TikTok-Live scale exceeds that). The 'Osprey + beava reference architecture' write-up + a docker-compose demo replaying the Bluesky firehose into Osprey-with-beava-counters is the obvious 6-week landing-page-anchor demo for this vertical.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Beava-side: NO public users on this use case yet [uncertain]; NO dedicated T&S / livestream demo identified in the repository as of the snapshot reviewed [uncertain] (closest analogues are python/beava/demos/fraud and python/beava/demos/ecommerce); NO beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads on T&S or livestream located yet [uncertain]. Beava knows WHO the buyer is (T&S Eng / Integrity Platform / Safety Signals teams at social, gaming, livestream, marketplace, dating; T&S-as-a-service vendors as embedders — correctly identified in the use-case write-ups). The ~60-primitive operator catalogue is a near-exact fit for the velocity / n_unique / distribution / distance feature shapes Bluesky-Osprey, Discord-Osprey, Twitch AutoMod, Reddit AutoModerator, Roblox Sentinel and Modulate ToxMod all consume. External validation that the SHAPE is right (not that beava itself has traction): (a) Osprey at Bluesky 45-50M events/day in production (ROOST blog, Sept 2025); at Discord 400M actions/day, 2.3M rules/sec, 204 action types, 2,288 rules (Discord engineering blog, InfoQ March 2026); explicit architecture statement that counters are NOT first-class — UDFs RPC out to external state services — and the Discord-internal Scylla-backed 'Counter service' was deliberately kept proprietary, leaving an Apache-2.0-shaped hole. (b) Bluesky 2025 transparency report: 41.4M users (up 60% YoY), 1.41B posts, 9.97M reports, 16.49M labels, 2.45M removals, 1,470 legal requests (up from 238 in 2024) — the velocity-feature backend pressure is enormous and Osprey-driven. (c) Roblox Sentinel open-sourced August 2025 with 1,200 NCMEC reports / 35% caught before user report Jan-Jun 2025; voice abuse reports/DAU cut in half — proves the shape and the open-source-T&S-tooling vector. (d) Modulate ToxMod at Call of Duty: BO6 repeat-offender rate -43%, Warzone -38%, ~2M voice-chat enforcement actions since Dec 2024 — proves the live-voice severity-aggregation primitive shape. (e) Bluesky's adoption of Osprey publicly cites 'reduced annual data-storage costs ~70%' vs prior solution — the buyer is actively migrating. (f) ROOST + Coop + Osprey July 2025 launch underwritten by Discord, Bluesky, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Roblox, MetaCAi (HMA donor), etc. — institutional momentum. (g) Market sizing: content moderation USD ~11.6-15B in 2025 with 13-15% CAGR through 2030-2031 (Mordor 14.4% CAGR; The Business Research Co. 14.5% CAGR; Research Nester ~13% to 2035; livestream/voice sub-segment 18.1% CAGR per Mordor; gaming/esports 16.95% CAGR). (h) Regulatory tailwind: EU DSA Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 transparency-report templates effective 1 July 2025 (first harmonised reports early 2026, 14 active VLOP investigations as of Nov 2025); UK OSA illegal-harms duties 17 March 2025, children's-safety duties 25 July 2025, Ofcom first £1M fine to AVS Group, Kick under formal investigation; EU CSAM derogation lapsed April 2026; KOSA US Senate-passed 2024 with bipartisan momentum; EU age-assurance guidelines for minors adopted 14 July 2025 with explicit live-streaming scope. Market validation is overwhelming; beava-specific traction is zero.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Lead. This is one of the strongest verticals in the matrix. Three converging signals: (1) the rules-engine layer just commoditised — Osprey is Apache-2.0, in production at Bluesky, with a Discord-scale provenance, and explicitly delegates counters to an external service, which is the exact shape beava ships; (2) regulatory tailwind is the strongest of any vertical — DSA Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 + UK OSA active enforcement (first fines issued, Kick investigation) + EU CSAM derogation gap + KOSA + EU minors guidelines, all in the last 18 months; (3) buyer roster is well-defined and reachable (Bluesky, Matrix.org, Mastodon hosts, mid-size livestream and gaming platforms, plus T&S-vendor embedders like Cinder, TrustLab, Lasso, Checkstep). The risk is execution: beava needs TLS+auth, triggers, prominently-promoted HLL/CMS/Top-K/T-Digest, multi-tenancy, and a published 'Osprey + beava' reference architecture with a working Bluesky-firehose-replay demo. The single highest-leverage move is to submit beava as a recommended counter/feature backend in the ROOST Osprey ecosystem — that route avoids competing with Cloudflare-style bundles and avoids the much harder fight of unseating Hive / ActiveFence / Modulate as classifiers. Pursue actively as a wedge; this is the cleanest 'sit underneath the rules engine, not against the classifier' play in the matrix.
